steps.title: Disconnect power
steps.body: Unplug the dishwasher or disconnect power before servicing. Replace all parts and panels before operating.
steps.sourceExcerpt: WARNING — Electrical Shock Hazard. Disconnect power before servicing.

steps.title: Diverter in Service Diagnostics
steps.body: Run Service Diagnostics — listen for spray zone changes or inspect diverter shaft rotation. Verify diverter disk installed.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Run Service Diagnostics — listen for spray zone changes or inspect diverter shaft rotation. Verify diverter disk installed.

steps.title: Disconnect P6 / measure at P7
steps.body: Power off. Unplug P6. Measure diverter motor at P7-4 and P7-6 (use P10-1 test pad for P7-4 per manual).
steps.sourceExcerpt: Power off. Unplug P6. Measure diverter motor at P7-4 and P7-6 (use P10-1 test pad for P7-4 per manual).

steps.title: Diverter motor 600–1800 Ω?
steps.body: Ohms between P7-4 and P7-6. Expected 600–1800 Ω.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Ohms between P7-4 and P7-6. Expected 600–1800 Ω.

steps.title: Continue after Service Diagnostics entry
steps.body: Service Diagnostics cycle should be available (entered via key sequence; cycle starts when door closes). Continue with bench checks below.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Refer to Component Testing; use Service Diagnostics Cycle for live load verification.

steps.title: Diverter rotates in Service Diagnostics?
steps.body: 120 VAC at P6-4 and P6-6 during diverter interval; motor must be connected.
steps.sourceExcerpt: 120 VAC at P6-4 and P6-6 during diverter interval; motor must be connected.

steps.title: Replace diverter assembly
steps.body: Replace diverter motor assembly if open/out of range.
steps.oemOutcome: Replace diverter motor assembly if open/out of range.

steps.title: Replace ACU
steps.body: Motor good but no AC output — replace control. If error persists, run diverter sensor test.
steps.oemOutcome: Motor good but no AC output — replace control. If error persists, run diverter sensor test.
